instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of rice until the water runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups of water, bring it to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave the lid on.
Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels and transfer them to a bowl. Sprinkle 1/4 tsp of the salt over them and toss.
In a large bowl, whisk 1/2 cup of the mayonnaise, the ketchup, the honey, the rice vinegar, the sugar and 1/4 tsp of the salt until smooth. This is the sauce.
In a second bowl, whisk the potato starch, the flour and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Add 3/4 cup of cold water and whisk until it's mostly smooth. A few lumps are fine.

Pour the oil into a deep skillet or wide pot, about 1 inch deep, and heat it over medium until it reaches 350°F. If you don't have a thermometer, drop in a bit of batter. It should sizzle and rise to the top right away.

Dip a shrimp in the batter, let the extra drip off, and lower it into the oil. Fry 10 shrimp at a time for about 2 minutes, turning once, until the coating is crisp and the shrimp are pink and curled. Don't crowd the pan.
Transfer the fried shrimp to a wire rack or a paper towel plate. Heat the oil back up and fry the rest in the same way.
Slice the scallions while the last batch fries.
Transfer all the shrimp to the bowl of sauce and toss gently so the coating stays on. Do this right before you serve.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Sprinkle the scallions and sesame seeds over the top. Serve with the rice.
method_notes: Cup of Yum's quick version (batter of potato starch and flour, 2 minutes in the oil, tossed in the sauce) is the lead. Its sauce uses sweetened condensed milk, so to keep this dairy-free the sauce follows Grumpy Recipes and Japanese Taste, which build the same creamy sweet sauce from mayonnaise, ketchup, honey and vinegar. Sources agree on a thin crisp coating and on tossing the shrimp in the sauce just before serving. They differ on the batter: Cup of Yum and Grumpy Recipes use a wet batter, Japanese Taste dusts the shrimp with plain cornstarch. The quantities are scaled up from Cup of Yum's 1 lb to suit a main dish.
